# Bio-Copilot

Bio-Copilot: An AI-native research assistant grounded in real-time PubMed data.

evidence_and_limit: Three-gene local slice/UniProt connector; unknown answer says deployment PubMed route, no actual real-time PubMed synthesis here.

text: It answers complex biological questions, simulates mutation-to-phenotype pathways, and generates structured scientific outputs like FASTA or PDB files.

text: Bio-Copilot evolves into a causal, multi-omic biological reasoning engine that operates as an execution layer over heterogeneous biomedical data and mechanistic models, rather than a retrieval-based assistant.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Rule graph/provenance output, no identified causal multi-omic execution engine.

text: At query time, it constructs a directed acyclic computation graph that links genomic loci to phenotypic endpoints via intermediate representations—variant annotation → transcript isoform selection → codon-level mutation mapping → protein structural perturbation → pathway flux redistribution → cellular state transitions.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: 4rule nodes annotation/structure/pathway/phenotype, no transcript isoform/codon mutation kinetic cascade.

text: Each node in this graph is parameterized by domain-specific models: variant impact is computed using ensemble predictors (VEP-like consequence classification, SIFT/PolyPhen-style deleteriousness priors), structural perturbation is approximated via ΔΔG estimation and local residue environment disruption (e.g., hydrogen bond network loss, electrostatic repulsion, metal coordination breakage), and pathway effects are propagated using constraint-based modeling (FBA) or ODE-based regulatory systems.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Hydrophobic/hotspot/domain ddG and scaled disruption, not structural Hbond/metal model or FBA/ODE model.

text: The system does not treat these as isolated modules; it performs cross-layer inference, ensuring that inconsistencies (e.g., structurally tolerated mutations with high pathway disruption) are explicitly flagged and reconciled.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Heuristic inconsistency flags, no actual cross-layer inference/reconciliation.

text: When answering a query, the system performs retrieval-augmented generation over a continuously updated literature index while simultaneously running programmatic reasoning pipelines—for example, mapping a mutation to its UniProt domain, identifying active-site residues, and simulating downstream signaling perturbations.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Known gene UniProt lookup code, no continuously updated literature index/RAG at query time.

text: This hybrid architecture overcomes a key limitation in current systems: purely neural models lack mechanistic grounding, while purely rule-based systems cannot generalize across incomplete data.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: No incomplete-data generalization superiority measured.

text: CRISPR design is implemented as a genome-scale optimization problem, where candidate guide RNAs are generated via exhaustive sliding-window enumeration over the target locus with PAM filtering (SpCas9 NGG/NAG, extended to Cas variants with alternative PAMs).
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Both-strandNGG local enumeration only, no NAG/other nuclease genome-scale optimization.

text: Each candidate is scored using a composite objective function incorporating GC content (optimal 40–60%), predicted on-target efficiency (sequence-dependent models), secondary structure folding energy (to avoid sgRNA hairpins), and off-target risk computed via genome-wide alignment with mismatch tolerance weighting in the seed region (positions 1–12 proximal to PAM).
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: GC/polyT/simple seed composition risk, no hairpin thermodynamics/whole-genome weighted alignment.

text: Chromatin accessibility priors (e.g., ATAC-seq derived openness) and epigenetic marks can be incorporated to refine cutting efficiency predictions.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Guide function has no chromatin/epigenetic input refinement.

text: For precise edits, the system dynamically selects between HDR, base editing, or prime editing by evaluating edit type constraints (transition vs. transversion), PAM proximity, and bystander edit risk, and then generates pegRNA designs with optimized primer binding site (PBS) lengths (typically 10–17 nt) and reverse transcriptase templates (10–20 nt) based on local sequence thermodynamics.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Transition/distance/bystander method rule and fixedPBS13/RTT16 labels, no actual pegRNA optimized sequences.

text: Gene regulatory networks are represented in SBML and solved using stiff ODE solvers for deterministic dynamics, while stochastic simulations (Gillespie SSA) capture transcriptional noise and low-copy-number effects.
